question.problem: Construct the vector field that has the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if the following equations hold:

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}
$$

Computing the partial derivatives of the function $ψ(x,y),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{∂ψ}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}) \\  & =2y{e}^{xy}+{y}^{2}x{e}^{xy} \\  & =y{e}^{xy}(2+yx), \\ Q & =-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x} \\  & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}) \\  & =-({y}^{3}{e}^{xy}+2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field with the stream function $ψ(x,y)={y}^{2}{e}^{xy}+{x}^{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & =P\,i+Q\,j \\  & =y{e}^{xy}(2+yx)\,i-({y}^{3}{e}^{xy}+2x)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
